newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Disney targets Africa through South African unit.
newsitem.headline: Disney targets Africa through South African unit.

text.p: The Walt Disney Co. launched a South African subsidiary Tuesday to consolidate its retail business here and explore avenues into the rest of Africa.
"The whole idea is to use South Africa as a base to go into the rest of Africa," Pierre Sissmann, president of Disney Consumer Products, Europe, Middle East and Africa, said in an interview.
"We don't know Africa. We don't know what the potential is. We have a lot to learn and we are here to do that."
Sissmann said the registration of Disney Enterprises Southern Africa was the international entertainment and franchise group's first foothold in Africa.
"We could have started in Francophone Africa, Senegal, and worked our way down, but we decided we would much rather start in South Africa and work our way north," he said.
Ray Botha, managing director of the South African subsidiary, said about 300 million rand ($66 million) worth of Disney products, mainly toys and textiles, were sold annually in South Africa.
Disney has been marketing in South Africa through licensees for more than 25 years, but has not previously had a registered presence in the country.
Sissmann said Disney would be on the look-out for unique cultural and marketing ideas that could be taken from South Africa into new markets.
He said the company would offer management support and the Disney license, but did not expect heavy capital investment in its South African partnerships.
